description: Strict prefixes of the generated remaps: gr (of gra, gri, grn and grr in Normal mode and gra in Visual mode), [ (of [d and [e) and ] (of ]d and ]e). Before the mapping timeout the engine waits for the rest of a mapping; after it, Vim runs the typed keys as built-in commands, and gr, [ and ] each still wait for a character or a second key.

cases.description: gr in Normal mode: a prefix of the gra, gri, grn and grr remaps, and after the timeout the built-in gr{char} that waits for a character.

vscodevim.deviation: Measured: on 2026-10-16, in VS Code 1.134.0 and 1.141.0 with VSCodeVim 1.32.4 and its default settings (harness of issue #11; spike/s2/data/fixture-reader-v2), when vim.timeout ran out after gr, VSCodeVim ran g and r as actions, found no gr action (vim.replaceWithRegister is off by default) and dropped both keys, in 30 of 30 trials at 10, 30 and 60 ms injected key delay. Vim's built-in gr{char} still waits for a character.

cases.description: [ in Normal mode: a prefix of the [d and [e remaps, and after the timeout the built-in [ prefix.
] in Normal mode: a prefix of the ]d and ]e remaps, and after the timeout the built-in ] prefix.
gr in Visual mode: a prefix of the gra remap, and after the timeout the built-in gr{char}, which in Visual mode replaces every selected character like r{char}.

vscodevim.deviation: Measured: on 2026-10-16, in VS Code 1.134.0 and 1.141.0 with VSCodeVim 1.32.4 and its default settings (harness of issue #11; spike/s2/data/fixture-reader-v2), when vim.timeout ran out after gr in Visual mode, VSCodeVim ran g and r as actions, found no Visual-mode gr action and dropped both keys, staying in Visual mode, in 30 of 30 trials at 10, 30 and 60 ms injected key delay. Vim's built-in gr{char} still waits for a character.
